**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Replace the invalid OpenROAD line ranges**

Anyone reopening C3-CLM-001 at this pinned URL cannot follow the recorded locator: [the referenced `TritonRoute.cpp`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/The-OpenROAD-Project/OpenROAD/b16bda7e82721d10566ff7e2b68f1ff0be9f9e38/src/drt/src/TritonRoute.cpp) has only 1,388 lines, so the range ending at 1,450 and the challenge's claimed 1,447–1,448 file-open check do not exist; the relevant `getDRCMarkers` and `reportDRC` code is instead around lines 980–1064 and 1295–1385. Because the verifier repeats these offsets, correct the source locator and every downstream citation, or pin the revision whose bytes actually match the reported ranges.

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Handle the absent review-followup manifest**

In a fresh checkout of this commit, `runs/GPT-COMPLIANCE-0004/public-review-followups.json` does not exist, and a repo-wide search finds no batch-0004 producer for it. Because `receipt()` reads it unconditionally for every one of the eight published PRs, the new publication audit raises `FileNotFoundError` before cloning and checking public bytes, even when there are simply no retained followups. Treat the missing file as an empty followup list, as the script already does for optional audit corrections, or publish the required manifest with this audit.
